key_insight: BoxMind converts continuous boxing bouts into precise, atomic punch events and uses a closed-loop expert system to optimize strategy; the pipeline was validated on elite competition at the 2024 Olympics, demonstrating practical tactical gains.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of structured tactical representations and closed-loop strategy optimization in combat sports analytics caused by complex spatio-temporal action dynamics and sparse high-quality validation.
method: Define atomic punch events with exact temporal boundaries and rich spatial/technical attributes to create a structured event representation.
Parse match video into an 18-category hierarchical technical taxonomy and extract sequence-level tactical patterns.
Close the loop by using the parsed signals for automated strategy optimization and field-validate recommendations during elite (2024 Olympic) competition.
impact: Provides a replicable pipeline for turning raw video into actionable tactics and closes the sim-to-field gap with real-world validation—useful for ML practitioners building interpretable, decision-focused systems for dynamic, adversarial domains.
visual_elements: Timeline/segmentation diagram showing raw video → atomic punch events with temporal boundaries
Hierarchical taxonomy tree (18 categories) mapping low-level punches to higher-level tactics
Closed-loop system diagram: perception → tactical model → strategy update → deployment
Performance/validation chart comparing pre/post-BoxMind tactical metrics or Olympic outcome improvements
paper_title: BoxMind: Closed-loop AI strategy optimization for elite boxing validated in the 2024 Olympics
paper_authors: Kaiwen Wang, Kaili Zheng, Rongrong Deng, Qingmin Fan, Milin Zhang
